messages.subject: Cut points for movisens data
parts:
Hi,

We are processing Movisens data (chest worn) using GGIR. The values for time spent in sedentary and light intensities seem unrealistically high. Is there a suggestion on which cut points to use for this device?

Thanks, Jo

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Cut points for movisens data
parts:
Hi Jo,

I had an e-mail conversation this week with someone asking the same question (same group?). Below I have copied a summary of the conversation to enable you and others to learn from my answers:

Question 27 June by student in Australia

We are presently using the Movisens EcgMove4 to capture movement in our study to determine how it may influence emotion regulation ability and the experience of psychological symptoms. The Movisens sensor is worn on the chest during a selected 12-hour waking period for 10 days.

Having processed the data, we've noticed the outputs show very high volumes of inactivity (around 89-95%) in a 18–65-year-old sample. I've attached an example output here (please note this output is from before applying the Eisgler 2011 modification). We've tried the Eisgler (2011) syntax modification (as below), but this resulted in no output for light, moderate or vigorous activity. We've tried changing the 'SampleRateInStudy' value to 64 (to match Movisens hz), using 'part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE, but still no output was produced for light, moderate or vigorous activity. I'm wondering if you might be able to provide any advice or assistance with this issue?


Response 28 June by me

Regarding the thresholds, I am now in doubt whether the information we have in the vignette is correct. The paper by Esliger was not very clear and did not come with code if I remember correctly. I now think we need to divide instead of multiply by 60. So, the calculation then becomes:

threshold.lig = ((LightCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

threshold.mod = ((ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

threshold.vig = ((VigorousCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000

mvpathreshold = ((ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins/sampleRateInStudy)/60) * 1000


which could be re-written in a more readable way as:


threshold.lig = (LightCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

threshold.mod = (ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

threshold.vig = (VigorousCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)

mvpathreshold = (ModerateCutPointFromPaper_in_gmins * 1000) / (sampleRateInStudy * 60)


I never used these equations myself and nobody provided feedback on this, so I assumed that people were happy with the equations.


Further, it may also be good for you to try out the other cut-points designed for data collected on the hip and compare results. If they all result in a high amounts of time spent in inactivity then this may indicate that hip cut points in general are not ideal for chest-worn sensors. If only some cut-points overestimate time in inactivity then it seems more likely that it is a study specific issue, e..g. they used a different calculation or they more calibration error in their data.


...

The conversation that followed clarified that their sleep estimates where problematic, most likely as a result of accelerometers not being worn. We then had some interaction about how to improve the sleep detection.


Kind regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
